title: KMS broker minimal-privilege matrix and escrow handling CONOPS
content:
Purpose:
This working CONOPS describes the minimum-privilege access model for the KMS broker (the service that mediates requests between Redwood services and customer-managed keys), the handling and retention model for tenant key escrow artifacts, and the set of audit log fields we need to guarantee SIEM compatibility and automated evidence extraction.

Audience:
Security engineers, infra engineers implementing RBAC v2 policies, SREs responsible for key lifecycle orchestration, compliance engineers building evidence automation pipelines, and solutions engineers onboarding BYOK customers.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- KMS broker must operate with narrowly scoped principals: service_read (encrypt/decrypt request pass-through without key material), service_sign (signing operations where allowed), admin_rotate (rotation orchestration), and escrow_manager (escrow-only ops).
- Escrow artifacts are treated as high-sensitivity audit material; retention is short by default (14 days hot, 365 days cold) and exportable only via signed evidence bundles to the customer or compliance team.
- Audit schema includes context that maps directly to SIEM fields: tenant_id, key_id, operation, actor_principal, actor_role, request_id, request_hash, kv_cache_hit, backend_response_latency_ms, hsm_slot_id, escrow_action, rotation_step, rotation_version_from, rotation_version_to, evidence_bundle_id.
- Evidence automation recipes (see playbook section) will periodically pull rotation-related events and materialize signed bundles for compliance retention and ad-hoc audits.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: RBAC v2 mapping for KMS broker principals and cross-service role bindings; audit schema for rotation and escrow; SIEM field mapping and an initial automation playbook for evidence export.
- Out-of-scope: full HSM integration design (assumes existing PKCS#11/HSM connector), detailed crypto algorithm decisions, customer-side key provisioning UX design.

Assumptions:
- The KMS broker is the single canonical mediator for all encrypted operations to customer-managed keys.
- All HSM interactions are logged with a correlation id (hsm_call_id) by the connector.
- RBAC v2 supports role-to-principal bindings, attribute-based conditions (e.g., service origin), and resource-scoped grants.

Definitions / roles (short):
- service_read: Allows encrypt/decrypt requests to be routed to KMS/HSM without exposing raw key material in the service plane. Does NOT allow rotation or escrow retrieval.
- service_sign: Allows sign/verify operations where customer policy permits (used by signing-only flows).
- admin_rotate: Orchestrates rotation workflows, bumping versions and triggering HSM keygen/fallover.
- escrow_manager: Can request generation of escrow artifacts and create/download evidence bundles; strictly audited and requires MFA-based approval in the console.
- auditor (read-only): Can read logs and evidence bundle metadata from the audit pipeline; cannot retrieve key material or escrow artifacts.

RBAC v2 mapping (conops guidance):
- Principle: Always prefer role-scoped resource grants rather than wide resource wildcards. Example bindings (expressed as plain tuples):
  - bind(service_a_instance, service_read, resource:tenant/abcd-1234/key/my-key)
  - bind(rotation-orchestrator-sa, admin_rotate, resource:tenant/*/key/*)
  - bind(escrow-service, escrow_manager, resource:tenant/abcd-1234/key/*, condition:only-from-ops-vpc)
  - bind(security_oncall, auditor, resource:tenant/*/key/*, time-window:08:00-18:00)
- Conditions: require network_source==private_ops_subnet for any admin_rotate or escrow_manager bindings.
- Policy lifecycle: roles and bindings must be provisioned via infra-as-code (terraform module kms_rbac_v2). Manual console grants are allowed only via an approval ticket (Jira KMS-5012) and must be time-limited.

Audit log schema (canonical fields for KMS events):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- tenant_id: opaque UUID
- key_id: hierarchical id (tenant/key-name/version?)
- operation: encrypt|decrypt|sign|verify|rotate|escrow-create|escrow-download|hsm-fallback
- request_id: tracing id propagated end-to-end
- actor_principal: service account or human user id
- actor_role: RBAC role used for the operation
- request_hash: SHA256 of the request payload (redacted) - to support tamper-evidence without exposing content
- response_code: internal result code (reference mapping below)
- backend_response_latency_ms: integer ms for HSM/KMS backend
- hsm_slot_id: if HSM used, the physical slot id or 'soft-kms'
- rotation_step: start|complete|fail|rollback
- rotation_version_from: previous key version id (nullable)
- rotation_version_to: new key version id (nullable)
- escrow_action: create|revoke|download (nullable)
- evidence_bundle_id: id when an evidence bundle is generated for export
- telemetry_tags: list of short tags for aggregation (e.g., batch, prefix-cache-hit)

Example audit event (single-line JSON example suitable for SIEM ingest):
{ "timestamp":"2024-11-02T13:17:09Z", "tenant_id":"t-41f7ee", "key_id":"t-41f7ee/k-774:1", "operation":"rotate", "request_id":"r-0a9f", "actor_principal":"svc-rotation-orch@infra", "actor_role":"admin_rotate", "rotation_step":"start", "rotation_version_from":"k-774:1", "rotation_version_to":"k-774:2", "backend_response_latency_ms":143, "hsm_slot_id":"hsm-03" }

SIEM export mapping (recommended target fields):
- siem.event.time <= timestamp
- siem.tenant.id <= tenant_id
- siem.kms.key_id <= key_id
- siem.user.id <= actor_principal
- siem.user.role <= actor_role
- siem.action <= operation
- siem.file.hash <= request_hash (when present)
- siem.kms.rotation.status <= rotation_step
- siem.kms.escrow.action <= escrow_action
- siem.kms.evidence.bundle_id <= evidence_bundle_id
- siem.duration.ms <= backend_response_latency_ms

Evidence automation playbook (high level steps):
1) Trigger: rotation events with rotation_step==complete OR escrow_action==create -> enqueue evidence job with request_id.
2) Collector pulls related audit events for request_id, key_id, tenant_id (lookback window 72h) and fetches any associated HSM audit receipts (hsm_call_id mapping).
3) Collate into an evidence bundle: metadata JSON (event list), signed receipts from HSM connector (if available), audit_log_snippet.txt, and a signed manifest (signed with platform evidence key).
4) Store bundle: hot store S3 (encrypted, KMS-managed) for 14 days; move to cold archival storage (WORM-like retention) for 365 days.
5) Automations: send a webhook to compliance pipeline and create Jira evidence ticket with bundle id if the event matches a compliance rule (e.g., tenant flagged).
6) Access: escrow_manager role can request download; downloads require an ephemeral one-time URL and an approval action (okta push or similar).

Automation implementation notes / gotchas:
- Evidence bundles must NOT contain unencrypted key material. If an HSM returns binary receipts that reveal keying material, the collector must reject and escalate.
- Use detached signatures (PKCS7/CMS) for manifests so they can be verified independently by auditors without needing the platform private key.
- Bundle size: rotation bundles may be large (HSM receipts + logs). Ensure the collector supports chunked upload to S3 and the SIEM ingest pipeline can accept metadata-only webhooks.

Rotation checklist (operational):
- Pre-check: confirm current key version reporting and active consumers (prometheus metric: kms.key_consumers{key_id})
- Staged rollout: create new key version in HSM, deploy rotation policy to service_read to allow both versions for 1 hour, monitor error rates and latency.
- Finalize: mark old version retired in registry, generate evidence bundle with rotation complete, create Jira artifact for compliance.
- Rollback: automated rollback path must be able to set the active pointer back to version_from; create rollback evidence bundle and mark rotation as failed in audit logs.

HSM fallback / failure scenarios (short):
- HSM unreachable: route to soft-kms read-only (if permitted by tenant policy) and mark operation as hsm-fallback in audit; trigger paging to infra oncall.
- HSM partial failure during rotation: pause rotation, do not mark version_to active, generate evidence bundle listing all HSM call ids and errors, escalate to engineering with priority P0.
- Escrow retrieval while under investigation: deny by default and require explicit exec approval (two-person approval) recorded in audit log.

BYOK onboarding and escrow handling (constrained flow):
- Customer provides key material or HSM details. escrow_manager must: validate key metadata, ensure tenant-side KMS policy indicates escrow_allowed==true, and schedule an escrow artifact generation window.
- Escrow artifacts are generated only with dual-signer (platform + escrow_manager) and must reference the customer-specified retention policy.
- De-provisioning: when tenant revokes escrow, mark the artifacts as revoked in the registry, rotate any derived platform-wrapped keys, and purge hot copies after 14 days. Cold copies remain under retention policy but flagged as revoked.

Operational recipes (quick commands and mappings for engineers):
- Audit query (search recent rotation starts without completes): query: operation:rotate AND rotation_step:start AND NOT rotation_step:complete within 48h -> create incident KMS-OP-ROT
- Evidence export (manual): POST /internal/v1/evidence/generate { request_id: r-XXXX } -> returns evidence_bundle_id and pre-signed S3 URL. Downloads require okta-two_factor and approval-id header.

Open questions / follow-ups before sign-off:
- Exact cold-retention SLA for escrow artifacts for regulated customers (default 365 days; should some industries require longer?)
- Should we allow service-level overrides for hsm-fallback to soft-kms during degraded mode? (security tradeoff)
- Do we standardize on CMS detached signatures or support multiple formats for cross-jurisdiction audits?

References and tickets:
- Jira: KMS-5012 (RBAC v2 terraform module), KMS-5098 (evidence-bundles feature), KMS-5133 (HSM connector receipts format)
- Confluence: SEC-KMS-CONOPS-1423 (design draft), SEC-EVIDENCE-SCHEMA (schema repo)
- Slack: #security-kms-ops for daily coordination

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally operational and prescriptive — expect follow-up PRs to the terraform kms_rbac_v2 module and a GH change to the KMS broker audit dispatcher.
- If you are an SRE reviewer, focus on the fallback and rotation rollback sections. If you are a compliance reviewer, focus on evidence retention and approval gating.

Unresolved action items:
- [ ] Decide cold-retention default for PII-bearing tenants (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2025-02-05)
- [ ] Implement time-limited console grants workflow (owner: Luca Alvarez, due: 2025-03-01)
- [ ] Add HSM receipt schema to SEC-EVIDENCE-SCHEMA and update collector (owner: Jordan Reed, due: 2025-01-28)

Last notes: this doc is a working-conops and should be iterated in public in the security confluence space. Once the terraform and collector PRs land, we will flip status to final and publish a shorter runbook for oncall use.
